newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria sacks board of directors of LNG company.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria sacks board of directors of LNG company.

text.p: The board of directors of Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas Limited (NLNG), which is handling an ambitious $4 billion gas project, has been dissolved, state radio reported on Saturday.

It said a statement issued by the office of oil minister Dan Etete on Friday night in the capital Abuja, said the dissolution took immediate effect and the company would now report directly to the oil ministry.
"The dissolution of the board lays to rest some unhealthy developments threatening the company's accountability," it said.
The four shareholders in the project are state oil firm Nigerian National Petreoleum Corp, Shell Sas BV, Elf Aquitaine and Agip SpA.
They are financing it solely from their own resources and have placed $2.873 billion in escrow accounts to execute the project.
The Nigerian statement said the project would deliver LNG in 1999 as scheduled.
